2608.19893.title: Interrupting the Loop: Periodic Subject Changes Raise Judged Surprise and Connection in Base Language Models
2608.19893.paper_summary: Where does the novelty a base language model produces with no task come from, and what can an LLM judge of a long stream actually see? We dismantle a cognitively inspired generation loop over 24 conditions on three base models. Most of its effect lives in one operation: a new subject injected every few hundred tokens (an interruption) into a stream whose literal repetition is damped (habituation). We judge windows of generated text only, with the premise as the unit (n=10) and a judge measured for repeatability, against a second judge family and against human readers. Under that protocol the interruption raises judged surprise by 1.2 to 1.4 points and connection by 0.8 over habituation alone. A connective that asks for continuity hurts; a bare paragraph break adds nothing detectable on fresh text; a reset context does at least as well as a kept one; and a pre-registered replication on new premises confirms the primary contrast. Three things the window judge could not see changed the first version of this study, and we think they are of general use. The judge scores the experimenter's injected sentence as the model's own. A fixed rotation of injected sentences makes the model replay its earlier segments from beyond the judge's horizon, and the judge scores the replay as surprise and connection (65-80% of post-interruption windows at periods 150-300). And the local gains do not compose: no arm produces an integrated document. The salience monitor, the in-loop judge, memory across interruptions and a judge-gated Review run with a gate that opens add nothing. On a problem with a verifier (online bin packing), the interruption multiplies valid, distinct candidate heuristics three- to fourfold without raising the quality of the best. We report an evaluation protocol for long generation and a controlled characterization of a simple intervention, not a mechanism of creativity.
2608.19893.paper_summary_zh: 新基礎語言模型在沒有任務的情況下產生的新穎性來自何處，而一個長串流中的大型語言模型實際上能看到什麼？我們在三個基礎模型上，對24種條件進行了一個認知啟發的生成迴路的拆解。其大部分效果存在於一個操作中：每幾百個標記注入一個新的主題（一次中斷）到一個字面重複被抑制的串流中（習慣化）。我們僅評估生成文本的窗口，以前提作為單位（n=10），並對重複性進行評估，與第二個評估者群體以及人類讀者進行比較。在該協議下，中斷使評估的驚訝度提高了1.2到1.4點，連結性提高了0.8，相較於僅有的習慣化。要求連續性的連結會造成傷害；一個簡單的段落斷裂對新文本沒有任何可檢測的影響；重置上下文的效果至少與保持的上下文一樣好；在新前提上進行的預註冊重複確認了主要對比。窗口評估者無法看到的三件事情改變了這項研究的第一個版本，我們認為它們具有普遍的用途。評估者將實驗者注入的句子評分為模型自己的句子。一個固定的注入句子輪換使模型重播其早期段落，超出評估者的視野，評估者將重播評分為驚訝和連結（在150-300的期間內，後中斷窗口的65-80%）。而當地的增益並不組合：沒有一個臂能產生一個整合的文檔。顯著性監控、迴路內評估者、跨中斷的記憶，以及一個帶有開啟閘門的評估者引導的回顧運行都沒有增加任何東西。在一個有驗證者的問題上（在線二進位打包），中斷使有效的、不同的候選啟發式增加三到四倍，而不提高最佳質量。我們報告了一個長生成的評估協議和一個簡單干預的受控特徵描述，而不是創造力的機制。
2608.19893.author: Roberto I. Ono Filho et.al.
